title: Best ATS and Recruiting CRMs With an MCP Server (2026): 8 Platforms Compared
summary: Which ATS and recruiting CRMs ship a native MCP server in 2026? Stardex compares 8 platforms on Claude and ChatGPT access, read/write scope, and setup.
body_markdown:
Compare eight ATS and recruiting CRMs with official MCP offerings, including Stardex. Review supported actions, permissions, setup, pricing, and team fit.


Executive search teams need recruiting context and controlled updates without repeatedly copying records into assistants. MCP servers connect assistants to database tools. As of October 21, 2026, vendor-published official offerings include Stardex, Recruit CRM, Loxo, Zoho Recruit (through Zoho MCP), Ashby (Beta), Greenhouse (open beta), Pinpoint, and Workable. We compare audience fit, supported actions, governance, setup, and commercial eligibility, distinguishing agency CRM needs from internal talent-acquisition candidate CRM and broader HR operations. Stardex is our first-place editorial recommendation for executive search firms, not a claim of exclusive MCP availability or independently established market leadership.


## **Why use an MCP server with an ATS or recruiting CRM?**


An MCP server is a standardized interface that exposes tools, resources, and prompts to compatible AI applications. For a recruiting database, it lets an assistant retrieve live, authorized records and invoke supported actions instead of relying exclusively on information pasted into a chat. Our Stardex MCP integration connects that interface to recruiting records, including people, companies, jobs, searches, tasks, and activity. The practical value is access to relevant database context while you work with an assistant—not an assumption that every connected assistant can change every record.


### **Which recruiting workflow problems can an MCP server address?**


-


**Repeated copy-and-paste:** Moving recruiting records into an assistant manually, rather than retrieving live context the authenticated user is authorized to access.


-


**Scattered candidate context:** Gathering candidate details and related search history across relevant recruiting records before assessing fit for a mandate.


-


**Recurring status preparation:** Bringing together active-search, pipeline, and recent-activity information to prepare a daily brief or search-status summary.


-


**Coordinating record updates:** Requesting changes from a chat while retaining user permissions and explicit approval, rather than assuming the assistant has unrestricted write access.


With Stardex, permission-aware search and approved actions connect these workflows to your recruiting database. You can request a candidate lookup with related search history, prepare an active-search brief, or request an approved update in chat. What happens depends on the available tools, authenticated-user permissions, and the AI client’s approval behavior. MCP availability does not mean universal write access, nor is it a security guarantee: authentication, authorization boundaries, scopes, and logging still need review. These are workflow examples—not evidence of measured time savings or error reduction—and recruiter judgment remains essential.


## **What should you look for in an ATS or recruiting CRM with an MCP server?**


Start with the recruiting workflow, not the integration badge. A firm managing client relationships and retained searches needs a different foundation from an internal talent acquisition team managing candidates for one employer. At Stardex, our executive-search offering combines ATS, CRM, outreach, and analytics with retained-search workflows and client-ready reporting. Then evaluate the named MCP implementation: who maintains it, which records it exposes, and what actions it permits. An official server and a community connector for the same platform can have materially different authentication and security properties.


### **Which five MCP capabilities should recruiting firms evaluate?**


1.


**Recruiting-firm fit.** Check agency client management, retained-search workflows, confidential candidate handling, and reporting—not just an internal candidate CRM. Our[executive-search offering](https://www.stardex.com/solutions/executive-search-solutions) documents retained fee models and configurable pipelines. Those platform capabilities establish audience fit; they do not establish which functions are exposed through MCP.


2.


**Verified record coverage and read/write tools.** Request an object-and-action list rather than assuming unrestricted create, read, update, and delete access. Stardex documents MCP search across people, companies, jobs, searches, tasks, activity, documents, and meetings. Writes depend on an available tool, user permission, and compatible client approval behavior. A REST API object’s availability does not establish its exposure through MCP.


3.


**Authentication and governance.** Ask how authentication, inherited permissions, scopes, approval controls, and logging work. Examine prompt-injection safeguards rather than treating MCP as a security guarantee—a risk addressed in[Greenhouse’s security documentation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/57182931313819-Greenhouse-MCP-security-FAQ) . Stardex documents remote OAuth authentication, but MCP-specific logging and other governance controls still need confirmation.


4.


**AI-client compatibility, setup, and ownership.** Verify support for your specific Claude or ChatGPT configuration and whether the implementation is official or community-built. Stardex’s official setup uses an organization-issued remote URL, client connector settings, authentication, and a read-only test before approved writes. One[community Ashby implementation](https://github.com/we-are-move/ashby-mcp-server) labels itself experimental and recommends Ashby’s official per-user OAuth server for production use—illustrating why the exact implementation matters.


5.


**Availability and total cost.** Confirm release stage, eligible subscriptions, connection charges, usage credits, and underlying platform pricing. Stardex’s MCP integration is documented as available now, but our public pricing page does not explicitly establish MCP plan eligibility. API access or webhook inclusion should not be treated as proof that MCP access is included.


For a 2026 shortlist, keep verified capabilities separate from unanswered purchasing and governance questions. Stardex documents an official remote OAuth MCP connection, recruiting-record search, and controlled two-way workflows; those are concrete evaluation points, not evidence of unrestricted database access. Before committing, confirm plan eligibility, any connection or usage charges, the exact write tools available to your team, and MCP-specific logging controls. We recommend starting with a known-record lookup, then testing approved writes in your chosen client before expanding the workflow to everyday search operations.


## **How can executive search teams use an MCP-enabled recruiting CRM?**


An executive search team can use Stardex’s MCP connection to bring authorized recruiting records into an AI-assisted workflow: prepare a search brief, rediscover candidates, review activity, or request a supported update. Our published integration scope supports the examples below; they are illustrative workflows, not tested customer outcomes or promises of autonomous execution. Start with retrieval, ask for record identifiers or references where available, and check generated summaries against the underlying records. Keep recruiter judgment central, especially when preparing client-facing material or approving changes to your database.


### **Strategy 1: Prepare a daily active-search brief**


Ask your assistant to summarize authorized active-search records before your morning review. Specify which searches to include and request supporting record references where available, so you can check the brief against the source rather than treating generated text as the definitive status.


-


**Authorized retrieval:** Use accessible active-search records to assemble a daily brief.


### **Strategy 2: Rediscover candidates against a search brief**


Provide the search brief and ask the assistant to surface relevant candidates from your authorized records. Review the suggested fit alongside available search history; a generated recommendation should support your assessment, not replace it.


-


**Candidate discovery:** Look for candidates against the requirements in a search brief.


-


**Related context:** Retrieve available candidate information and related search history to inform your review.


### **Strategy 3: Draft a client-ready candidate summary**


Request a draft based on authorized candidate records, with supporting references where available. Before sharing it with a client, verify every substantive statement against the underlying records and review what information is appropriate to disclose. Treat “client-ready” as the editorial goal—not permission to send an unchecked draft.


-


**Reviewed drafting:** Generate a candidate summary from accessible records, then have a recruiter check accuracy, relevance, and confidentiality before client use.


### **Strategy 4: Review pipeline activity and follow-ups**


Ask for a search-status summary alongside recent activity and available task or meeting context. Use the response to identify follow-ups that need your attention, then check the underlying records before deciding what to do next.


-


**Live search-status summaries:** Review the current search information available through the connection.


-


**Recent-activity reviews:** Summarize recorded activity to prepare for a pipeline discussion.


-


**Task and meeting context:** Consult accessible tasks and meetings when reviewing outstanding work.


### **Strategy 5: Request an approved record update**


Move from retrieval to updates only after confirming the relevant write tool exists. State the intended change clearly and require explicit approval before execution. Our public documentation does not provide an exhaustive field-level write matrix, so confirm the supported operation rather than assuming any record or field can be changed.


-


**Controlled write access:** Use an available write tool within the authenticated user’s permissions and with compatible client approval behavior.


### **Strategy 6: Connect and validate an AI assistant**


In Stardex, open **Settings > Integrations** and copy your organization-issued remote MCP URL and authentication instructions. Add Stardex through the compatible AI client’s connector settings and authenticate. For supported OpenAI clients or Responses API applications, select allowed tools and approval behavior; do not assume every OpenAI experience supports the same access.


-


**Organization-specific connection:** Use your issued MCP URL and Stardex OAuth, with connector access governed by workspace permissions.


-


**Read-only validation first:** Look up a known person or search, verify the result, and only then enable supported writes with explicit approval.


These workflow categories are not exclusive to Stardex; the reason to consider us for executive search is the recruiting context behind the connection. Our executive-search offering combines ATS, CRM, outreach, and analytics with retained-search workflows, confidential candidate handling, configurable pipelines, retained fee models, and client-ready reporting. Evaluate the MCP connection against that operational fit, then validate the tools your team actually needs. Keep source checks, human review, and explicit update approval in the process rather than assuming a successful connection makes every output ready to use.


## **How do the eight ATS and recruiting CRM MCP offerings compare?**


All eight platforms below have official vendor-published MCP evidence in 2026; none should be dismissed as community-only. Our ordering prioritizes recruiting agencies and executive search workflows, rather than reflecting a hands-on performance benchmark. The first four options address agency-oriented recruiting databases; the remaining platforms primarily serve internal hiring, sometimes with candidate CRM functionality. Compare the actual tools, permissions, setup requirements, and subscription eligibility—not simply whether an MCP connection exists. “Not established” means public documentation does not confirm a detail, not that the platform lacks that capability.


#### **Stardex**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** ATS + CRM; executive search and recruiting firms.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Native remote MCP; available now.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Search people, companies, jobs, searches, tasks, activity, documents, and meetings. Controlled record updates require an available write tool, user permission, and compatible client approval behavior; exhaustive write matrix not published.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT; homepage also names Manus and Gemini. Gemini access is interface-specific.


-


**Authentication:** Stardex OAuth.


-


**Setup:** Settings → Integrations; copy the organization-issued URL and instructions, add the connector, authenticate, and test a known record read-only before approved writes.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** MCP plan eligibility and MCP-specific fees are not established. API availability does not establish MCP eligibility.


#### **Recruit CRM**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Agency ATS + CRM, including client and candidate workflows.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official remote MCP; current OAuth connection replaces older API-key connections.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Read candidates, jobs, companies, contacts, tasks, meetings, notes, call logs, and hotlists. Create and update records on explicit request; no delete actions. Role-selectable Read Only or Read & Write access.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity.


-


**Authentication:** User-role-scoped OAuth; Account Owners and Admins retain Read & Write access.


-


**Setup:** Enable MCP Access under Admin Settings → User → Roles & Permissions; select access level, connect the assistant, and authorize. Replace old API-key connections.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Business and Enterprise. Confirm current subscription pricing and any MCP-specific charges.


#### **Loxo**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Agency-oriented recruiting platform with CRM-relevant deals and placements.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official agency-scoped MCP connection; published as available.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Covers people, jobs, companies, deals, placements, scorecards, and campaigns. Users control read/write permissions; exact individual write tools are not established.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude Desktop, Claude web, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor.


-


**Authentication:** OAuth with an agency-scoped MCP URL.


-


**Setup:** Add the agency-specific URL to the client, sign in, and select permissions. Available capabilities remain plan-dependent.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Professional and above; no extra connection charge. Credit-consuming Loxo Agents still use credits through MCP. Confirm subscription pricing.


#### **Zoho Recruit**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Recruiting platform with separate Staffing Agency and Corporate HR editions; agency edition includes client and candidate relationship management.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official integration through the shared Zoho MCP service; configurable tool selection.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Retrieve candidates and notes; search related records; update candidate status; cancel interviews; delete candidates. Normally exclude destructive tools unless explicitly required.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT, Windsurf, Cursor, VS Code.


-


**Authentication:** OAuth connects Recruit to Zoho MCP.


-


**Setup:** Create/open a Zoho MCP server → Tools → Add Tools → Zoho Recruit; select required tools and copy the Connect endpoint into the client.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Zoho MCP is currently described as free; normal service API limits apply. Recruit subscription costs remain separate; Recruit edition eligibility is not established.


#### **Ashby**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Internal-hiring ATS with sourcing, candidate CRM, scheduling, and analytics—not automatically an agency deal/placement CRM.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official MCP Beta.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Reads supported; create candidates, add notes with confirmation, change application stages, and add candidates to jobs. Tool contracts may change.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Glean, Gemini CLI.


-


**Authentication:** Per-user OAuth.


-


**Setup:** Org Admin enables MCP under Organization Setup → Opt-In Features; connecting users need Elevated Access, then connect and authorize.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Recruiting plans; Analytics-only organizations excluded. Confirm current pricing. Ashby recommends its public API for stable integrations.


#### **Greenhouse**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Internal-hiring ATS with sourcing CRM, prospect pools, structured interviews, and scorecards.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official, vendor-maintained MCP open beta.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Reads and writes constrained by supported tools, organization-approved scopes, and user permissions. Specific mutation examples are not established in public documentation.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT, Google Antigravity, Glean, Copilot Studio, Amazon Q, Grok AI.


-


**Authentication:** OAuth 2.0 PKCE; Dynamic Client Registration compatibility.


-


**Setup:** Site Admin configures Dev Center → MCP Access; users authorize using environment-specific client instructions. Scope changes require reconnection.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Core, Plus, Pro. Legacy-tier eligibility and pricing require confirmation with the account team.


#### **Pinpoint**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** In-house talent acquisition ATS with a built-in talent pipeline CRM.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official first-party MCP V2, released June 2026; current OAuth architecture supersedes the original header-based setup.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Permission-respecting queries and action tools, including moving candidates; reporting, outreach drafting, and candidate rediscovery.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude Desktop explicitly documented; other compatible MCP clients supported. Additional V2 client-specific instructions are not established.


-


**Authentication:** OAuth.


-


**Setup:** Admin enables the self-service toggle; users connect through OAuth. One-click Claude Desktop setup; original users should upgrade to V2.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** MCP plan eligibility and pricing are not established. Do not apply the original API-header limitations to V2.


#### **Workable**


-


**Platform category and audience fit:** Recruiting and HR operations platform; fit centers on internal hiring and employee workflows.


-


**Official MCP architecture and availability stage:** Official remote MCP using Streamable HTTP.


-


**Verified reads and write examples:** Read/write access inheriting user permissions. Catalog covers jobs, candidates, offers, requisitions, employees, time off, time tracking, and performance reviews; specific mutation examples are not established here.


-


**Documented AI clients:** Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot.


-


**Authentication:** OAuth2; no manually managed API keys.


-


**Setup:** Add the remote connector and authorize; discover accounts with \`get_accounts\`, then use the selected account subdomain.


-


**Plan eligibility and pricing caveats:** Newer guidance specifies paid plans. An earlier announcement says no additional MCP charge; confirm current terms and trial access.


For executive search firms, we prioritize Stardex’s recruiting-record access and controlled updates; our[MCP documentation](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) explains the organization-specific connection process. Recruit CRM and Loxo are substantive agency alternatives, while Zoho Recruit adds configurable tools through its shared MCP service. Internal talent acquisition teams should also consider Ashby, Greenhouse, Pinpoint, and Workable without confusing candidate CRM with agency business development. Before rollout, review[Recruit CRM’s permission model](https://help.recruitcrm.io/en/articles/14485570-recruit-crm-mcp-model-context-protocol) and[Ashby’s enablement requirements](https://docs.ashbyhq.com/ashby-mcp-server-beta) , then confirm your chosen vendor’s current plan eligibility, client support, and permitted write tools.


## **Which are the best ATS and recruiting CRMs with an MCP server in 2026?**


For recruiting firms, the first distinction is audience fit: Stardex, Recruit CRM, Loxo, and Zoho Recruit offer agency-relevant ATS and CRM capabilities. Ashby, Greenhouse, and Pinpoint combine internal-hiring ATS workflows with candidate CRM functionality; Workable spans recruiting and HR. These are not interchangeable with an agency’s client-development and retained-search CRM.


### **1. Stardex**


Our native MCP server connects your recruiting database to Claude, supported OpenAI clients, and other compatible assistants through remote OAuth authentication. Recruiters can search people, companies, jobs, searches, tasks, activity, documents, and meetings without moving that context into a separate spreadsheet. Supported writes depend on available tools, the authenticated user’s permissions, and the client’s approval behavior—not simply on having a connection. For executive search teams, the practical value is bringing existing candidate intelligence and live search context into the assistant they already use, while keeping updates controlled.


Stardex is our first-place recommendation for retained-search and recruiting firms because we combine an AI-native ATS and CRM with executive-search workflows, confidential candidate handling, and client-ready reporting. That recommendation rests on audience fit—not exclusive MCP availability or a claim of market leadership.


**Key Features**


-


**Remote OAuth MCP:** An official, native connection rather than a community-maintained wrapper.


-


**Permission-aware access and supported writes:** Recruiting-record access and approved actions respect user permissions and available tools.


-


**Executive-search workspace:** ATS, CRM, outreach, and analytics support retained searches and relationship-driven recruiting.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


**Candidate discovery:** Find relevant people against a search brief using existing recruiting records.


-


**Search-status and activity summaries:** Review live search progress and recent interactions.


-


**Approved updates and reporting:** Use supported record-update tools and reporting workflows with appropriate permissions and approvals.


**Pricing**


-


Starter and Pro have published per-user pricing; Copilot uses custom pricing. Check the current billing selection on the pricing page before comparing amounts.


-


API access and exports are listed across plans, with webhooks in Pro. Neither establishes MCP plan eligibility, which requires confirmation.


**Pros**


-


Retained-search workflows, retained fee models, and confidential candidate handling.


-


Custom fields, configurable pipelines, and client-ready reporting.


**Cons**


-


Public documentation does not establish an exhaustive write-tool matrix or MCP eligibility by plan.


-


Available actions depend on the AI client, workspace permissions, and approval configuration.


**Setup:** Open Settings > Integrations, copy your organization-issued MCP URL and authentication instructions, add the connector in your AI client, and authenticate. Test a known person or search with a read-only lookup before enabling approved writes.


Our distinction is the combination of[executive-search workflows](https://www.stardex.com/solutions/executive-search-solutions) and a[native MCP connection](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) . Review the specific[Claude](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/claude) or[OpenAI](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/openai) instructions alongside[current pricing](https://www.stardex.com/pricing) to validate the connection, permissions, and commercial terms for your firm.


### **2. Recruit CRM**


Recruit CRM is a direct agency ATS-plus-CRM alternative with an official remote MCP server. Its connection covers recruiting records alongside company and contact information, making it relevant to firms managing both candidate pipelines and client relationships. Authentication now uses role-scoped OAuth rather than the older account-wide API-key approach. Administrators can choose Read Only or Read & Write access, while Account Owner and Admin roles retain Read & Write access. Its documented assistant setup covers Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity, with writes performed only when explicitly requested.


**Key Features**


-


User-role-scoped OAuth with selectable Read Only or Read & Write access.


-


Coverage includes candidates, jobs, companies, contacts, tasks, meetings, notes, call logs, and hotlists.


-


Official instructions cover Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity; other clients need remote OAuth MCP over Streamable HTTP.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


Candidate and job lookups, plus pipeline analysis.


-


Explicit-request creation and updates across supported records; delete actions are excluded.


-


Setup: enable MCP Access under Admin Settings > User > Roles & Permissions, select the access level, then connect through a supported assistant or \`https://agent.recruitcrm.io/mcp\` and authorize with OAuth.


**Pricing**


-


MCP is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Confirm current subscription amounts with Recruit CRM.


**Pros**


-


Substantive agency candidate, client, and pipeline coverage.


-


Role-based access provides a clear distinction between lookup-only and write-enabled use.


**Cons**


-


No delete actions through MCP.


-


Plan restrictions apply, and old API-key connections must be deleted and reconnected using OAuth.


Resources:[official MCP documentation](https://help.recruitcrm.io/en/articles/14485570-recruit-crm-mcp-model-context-protocol) and[recruiting workflow coverage](https://recruitcrm.io/features/recruit-crm-mcp/) .


### **3. Loxo**


Loxo’s official MCP offering connects assistants to recruiting and business-development context through an agency-scoped URL and OAuth sign-in. Its coverage includes people, jobs, companies, deals, placements, scorecards, and campaigns, giving agency teams more than candidate lookup alone. Users control read-versus-write permissions, while their subscription determines which capabilities are exposed. Documented clients include Claude Desktop, Claude web, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor. Published workflows range from candidate briefs and longlists to stalled-pipeline checks, but teams should confirm individual write tools rather than infer unrestricted record management.


**Key Features**


-


Agency-scoped connection URL with OAuth authentication.


-


User-controlled read/write permissions and plan-bound capabilities.


-


Recruiting and business-development objects, including deals and placements, with bidirectional activity context.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


Candidate briefs, longlists, and stalled-pipeline checks.


-


Re-engagement drafts and data-hygiene workflows.


-


Setup: add the agency-scoped MCP URL to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or another compatible assistant, then sign in through OAuth and configure permissions.


**Pricing**


-


MCP is included with Professional plans and above without an extra connection charge.


-


Credit-consuming Loxo Agents still consume credits through MCP. Confirm current subscription pricing separately.


**Pros**


-


Agency-specific context includes deals and placements alongside recruiting records.


-


Documented support spans several assistant interfaces.


**Cons**


-


Available capabilities remain limited by the subscription.


-


Agent credit usage still applies, and tool-level write coverage requires confirmation.


Resource:[Loxo’s official MCP offering](https://loxo.co/products/loxo-mcp) .


### **4. Zoho Recruit**


Zoho Recruit connects through the official Zoho MCP service, rather than a standalone Recruit-specific server or a community-only wrapper. Teams create a server in that shared service, select Recruit tools, and authenticate through OAuth. This architecture allows a deliberately narrow connection or a broader cross-application configuration, depending on the tools selected. Recruit offers separate Staffing Agency and Corporate HR editions, so audience fit depends on the underlying product choice. Documented MCP actions include candidate-status changes and candidate deletion, making careful tool selection especially important before enabling writes.


**Key Features**


-


OAuth authentication and selectable tools within the shared Zoho MCP service.


-


Staffing Agency and Corporate HR editions; the agency edition includes client handling and configurable pipelines.


-


Zoho names Claude, ChatGPT, Windsurf, Cursor, and VS Code as compatible clients.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


Retrieve candidates and notes, and search related records.


-


Update candidate status, cancel interviews, and delete candidates through documented tools.


-


Setup: create or open a Zoho MCP server, choose Tools > Add Tools > Zoho Recruit, select only necessary tools, authenticate, and copy the Connect endpoint into the AI client.


**Pricing**


-


Zoho MCP is currently free to use; the underlying Recruit subscription is separate.


-


Connected services’ normal API limits still apply. Confirm Recruit subscription pricing independently.


**Pros**


-


An agency edition supports client relationships, formatted resumes, pipelines, and reporting.


-


Configurable tools can combine recruiting with other connected Zoho applications.


**Cons**


-


The shared service adds a configuration step beyond enabling Recruit alone.


-


Destructive tools require deliberate restriction; exclude candidate deletion unless the workflow explicitly needs it.


Resources:[Recruit integration and setup](https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/recruit/integrations/zoho-apps/zoho-mcp/articles/zoho-recruit-integration-with-zoho-mcp) ,[Zoho MCP FAQ](https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/mcp/help-support/articles/zoho-mcp-faq) , and[Staffing Agency edition](https://www.zoho.com/recruit/staffing-agency-software.html) .


### **5. Ashby**


Ashby combines an ATS, sourcing and candidate CRM, scheduling, and analytics for internal talent acquisition teams, from startups to enterprises. Its official MCP server is in beta and uses per-user OAuth. Access requires organization-level enablement and Elevated Access for connecting users, rather than simply possession of an account. Alongside reads, Ashby documents specific writes, including candidate creation and application-stage changes. Its candidate CRM supports talent relationships, but should not be treated as equivalent to an agency’s client-development, deal, and placement CRM when evaluating recruiting-firm fit.


**Key Features**


-


Official MCP Beta with per-user OAuth.


-


Org Admin enablement and Elevated Access requirements.


-


Documented compatibility with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Glean, Gemini CLI, and compatible clients.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


Read recruiting information and create candidates.


-


Add candidate notes with confirmation, change application stages, and add candidates to jobs.


-


Setup: enable Admin > Organization Setup > Opt-In Features > MCP Server, connect the client to \`https://mcp.ashbyhq.com/mcp/v1\`, and complete OAuth.


**Pricing**


-


MCP access is offered across recruiting plans, excluding Analytics-only organizations. Confirm subscription amounts with Ashby.


**Pros**


-


Integrated internal-hiring workflows spanning sourcing, scheduling, and analytics.


-


Specific documented write actions make supported workflows easier to assess.


**Cons**


-


Beta tool contracts may change; Ashby recommends its public API for stable integrations.


-


Candidate CRM functionality is not evidence of agency client-development or deal-management coverage.


Resources:[official MCP Beta documentation](https://docs.ashbyhq.com/ashby-mcp-server-beta) and[Ashby’s platform overview](https://www.ashbyhq.com/) .


### **6. Greenhouse**


Greenhouse combines structured hiring with sourcing CRM, including prospect creation and prospect pools. Its official, vendor-maintained MCP server is in open beta and supports reads and writes within approved scopes, available tools, and existing user permissions. A Site Admin controls the organization’s scope configuration before users authorize their accounts. Claude and ChatGPT are among the documented clients, but setup depends on the customer’s environment. For comparison purposes, Greenhouse belongs in the internal-hiring group: its candidate CRM should not be confused with an agency’s business-development and retained-search CRM.


**Key Features**


-


OAuth 2.0 PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration compatibility.


-


Site Admin-approved scopes with existing-user permission boundaries.


-


Supported clients include Claude, ChatGPT, Google Antigravity, Glean, Copilot Studio, Amazon Q, and Grok AI.


**Recruiting MCP Offerings**


-


Recruiting-data reads and supported writes, constrained by tools, scopes, and user permissions.


-


Verify the current tool catalog for individual actions; a read/write designation does not establish every possible update.


-


Setup: configure Dev Center > MCP Access, then follow environment-specific client instructions and authorize the user account. Do not assume the US endpoint applies universally.


**Pricing**


-


Core, Plus, and Pro subscriptions are eligible. Legacy-tier access and current pricing require account-team confirmation.


**Pros**


-


Structured interview kits, scorecards, scheduling, and reporting.


-


Sourcing CRM with prospects and prospect pools.


**Cons**


-


Open-beta status and legacy-plan eligibility caveats.


-


Scope changes require reconnection; individual write actions need verification.


Resources:[Greenhouse MCP documentation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/52090956642075-Greenhouse-MCP) ,[environment-specific setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/52096319906971-Set-up-Greenhouse-MCP-with-supported-AI-tools) , and[platform capabilities](https://www.greenhouse.com/pricing) .


### **7. Pinpoint**


Pinpoint is built for in-house talent acquisition, with hiring coverage from planning and attraction through selection and onboarding, plus a built-in talent pipeline CRM. Its first-party MCP V2, released in June 2026, uses OAuth and provides permission-respecting query and action tools. An administrator enables the connection through a self-service toggle, and Claude Desktop has a one-click setup path. Current documentation describes candidate movement, reporting, outreach drafting, and rediscovery. Its audience fit is corporate recruiting operations rather than the client-development and retained-search requirements of an executive search firm.


**Key Features**


-

## **FAQs about ATS and recruiting CRM MCP servers**


### **Why do recruiting firms need an MCP-enabled ATS or CRM?**


An MCP connection is useful when recruiters want an AI assistant to retrieve live, authorized recruiting records and perform supported actions without repeatedly pasting database context. It is a workflow option, not a requirement for every firm. With Stardex, for example, our Claude integration supports candidate discovery against a search brief, live search-status summaries, and recent-activity reviews. Those workflows bring existing recruiting knowledge into the conversation while preserving permission controls. Start with a recurring research or reporting task, then consider approved updates only where the server and client support them.


### **What is an MCP server for an ATS or recruiting CRM?**


An MCP server exposes tools, resources, and prompts through a standardized interface that compatible AI applications can use. For an ATS or recruiting CRM, that lets an assistant retrieve live records and invoke specifically supported actions, rather than work only from information pasted into a conversation. Stardex uses an official remote MCP server with OAuth authentication for access to recruiting data. MCP is not unrestricted API access: an update still needs an available write tool, the authenticated user’s permission, and compatible approval behavior in the AI client.


### **Which recruiting CRMs have an official MCP server in 2026?**


All eight platforms in this comparison document official MCP offerings in their public 2026 documentation: Stardex, Ashby, Greenhouse, Recruit CRM, Pinpoint, Workable, Zoho Recruit, and Loxo. Zoho Recruit connects through the shared Zoho MCP service, rather than a separate Recruit-only server. For recruiting CRM evaluation, distinguish agency relationship-management needs from ATS-focused hiring workflows; Recruit CRM explicitly covers both ATS and CRM records. We recommend Stardex for executive search and contingent firms because of that audience fit—not because every official MCP offering serves the same recruiting model or exposes identical actions.


### **Which ATS and recruiting CRM MCP servers can update records?**


Stardex supports controlled two-way workflows, with updates dependent on available tools, user permissions, and client approval behavior. Ashby documents candidate creation, notes with confirmation, application-stage changes, and adding candidates to jobs. Recruit CRM supports creation and updates on explicit request but excludes deletes. Zoho Recruit exposes status changes alongside destructive tools such as candidate deletion; normally exclude destructive tools unless explicitly needed. Greenhouse, Pinpoint, Workable, and Loxo also document actions or write access, but confirm each platform’s current tool scope, permissions, and client-specific approval controls before enabling changes.


### **How do you connect Stardex to Claude or a supported OpenAI application?**


In Stardex, open **Settings > Integrations** and copy your organization-issued remote MCP URL and authentication instructions. Add Stardex through the compatible AI client’s connector settings, then complete Stardex OAuth authentication. In supported OpenAI clients or Responses API applications, configure allowed tools and approval behavior where available; Claude workspace permissions also govern connector approval. First test a read-only lookup against a known person or search. Enable approved updates only after that succeeds. Confirm your client’s current connector requirements: our documentation does not establish identical actions across every Claude or ChatGPT interface or subscription.


### **Are Ashby and Greenhouse MCP servers still in beta?**


Yes—in its public 2026 documentation, Ashby’s official MCP server is labeled **Beta** , and Greenhouse’s vendor-maintained server is in **open beta** . Ashby requires organization-level enablement and Elevated Access for connecting users; its documentation warns that tool contracts may change and recommends its public API for stable integrations. Greenhouse access remains subject to supported tools, organization-approved scopes, and existing permissions. By contrast, our Stardex documentation describes MCP as available now. That is an availability statement, not a claim of formal general-availability certification. Recheck both competitors’ beta status before procurement.


### **Is Zoho Recruit MCP a separate server or part of Zoho MCP?**


Zoho Recruit connects through the official shared **Zoho MCP** service, not a separate Recruit-only offering or a required self-hosted community wrapper. Sign in to Zoho MCP, create or open a server, choose **Tools > Add Tools** , select Zoho Recruit, and add only the tools you need. Authenticate through OAuth, then copy the endpoint from **Connect** into your compatible AI client. Stardex instead provides our own official remote MCP integration. Zoho says its MCP service is currently free, but Recruit subscription charges and connected-service API limits still apply.


### **Which subscription plans include recruiting MCP access?**


Documented eligibility includes Recruit CRM Business and Enterprise; Loxo Professional and above; Workable paid plans; and Ashby recruiting plans, excluding Analytics-only organizations. Greenhouse lists Core, Plus, and Pro, while legacy-tier customers must contact their account team and confirm access and pricing. Loxo has no extra MCP connection charge, but credit-consuming Agents still use credits through MCP. Confirm Stardex and Pinpoint MCP eligibility directly: our Stardex pricing page does not explicitly establish it. Zoho MCP’s free service does not make Zoho Recruit free. Recheck current terms and client subscription requirements before purchase.
